questions.q: What is a virtual warehouse in Snowflake?
options: A named cluster of compute resources that runs queries against the storage layer, with no data of its own
A physical server rack dedicated to one customer
A synonym for a Snowflake database
A tool for backing up data to another cloud provider
questions.explain: A virtual warehouse provides compute only — CPU, memory, and temp storage — and reads from the separate storage layer without owning any data itself.

questions.q: What is the warehouse size scale, and roughly what happens each step up?
options: X-Small through 6X-Large, roughly doubling compute resources (and credits per hour) at each step
Small, Medium, Large only, with no cost difference between them
1 through 10, where size has no effect on cost
A single fixed size that cannot be changed
questions.explain: Warehouse size follows a T-shirt scale from X-Small to 6X-Large, with compute resources and hourly credit cost roughly doubling at each step.

questions.q: What do auto suspend and auto resume do?
options: Auto suspend stops a warehouse after N minutes of inactivity (costing nothing while suspended); auto resume automatically restarts it when a new query needs it
Auto suspend permanently deletes a warehouse; auto resume recreates it from scratch
They control how large a warehouse can grow, not whether it's running
They only apply to the storage layer, not compute
questions.explain: This pair is what makes 'pay only for compute you use' real: an idle warehouse suspends and stops costing credits, then resumes automatically within seconds when needed again.

questions.q: What problem do multi-cluster warehouses solve?
options: Concurrency — queries queuing up because too many are running at once, solved by adding more same-size clusters automatically
Making a single query run faster by using a bigger warehouse size
Reducing the amount of storage a database uses
Automatically backing up data to a second region
questions.explain: Multi-cluster warehouses add or remove clusters of the same size based on concurrent query demand — a different problem from resizing, which speeds up individual queries.

questions.q: Fifty analysts hit dashboards at the same time and queries start queuing. What's the right fix?
options: Enable multi-cluster on the warehouse so more clusters can handle the concurrent load
Resize the warehouse to a larger single size
Disable auto-suspend entirely
Create a new database for each analyst
questions.explain: Queuing under high concurrency is a multi-cluster problem, not a size problem — resizing makes individual queries faster but doesn't let more queries run at once.
